channel.title: CarbonXFuture Insights
channel.description: Weekly desk notes and analysis on waste-oil carbon credits, base oil markets, voluntary carbon pricing and regulation — from the CarbonXFuture desk in Fort Lauderdale.

item.title: Waste Oil Recycling: The Fastest-Growing Slice of a $50 Billion Market
item.description: The recycling market grows from $4.29B (2026) to $7.13B by 2035 at 5.8% CAGR — faster than the waste oil market overall. Value is migrating from disposal to processing.

item.title: The $50 Billion Waste Oil Opportunity: Market Outlook to 2033
item.description: The global waste oil market grows from $36.2B (2026) to $49.9B by 2033 — yet 42.6% of waste oil is still landfilled. What the numbers mean for collectors, re-refiners and carbon markets.

item.title: Desk Note: EUAs Test a Breakout, Re-refiners Sold Out
item.description: EU allowances hit a nine-day high before fading, VCM issuance quality improves as supply shrinks, and US base oil postings rise again with re-refined barrels fully committed.

item.title: Desk Note: Tight Base Oils, Steady Carbon
item.description: ACCUs stall above A$38 and Verra issuance ticks along, while Middle East outages keep US base oils on allocation and re-refiners effectively sold out.

item.title: Introducing CXF: how waste oil recycling generates traceable carbon credits
item.description: Why the most overlooked stream in the circular economy deserves its own carbon standard — and how the CXF framework works, from evidence to serialized units.

item.title: How many carbon credits does a gallon of used oil generate? The CXF factors, explained
item.description: 10.8, 19.3 and 25.7 tCO2e per 1,000 gallons — where the CXF quantification factors come from, the EPA and ACR/IPCC anchors they sit between, and what evidence turns volumes into credits.

item.title: How voluntary carbon credits are priced: a buyer's primer
item.description: Why one tonne of CO2 trades at $9 and another at $31 — project type, vintage, co-benefits, integrity labels, and how to read an indicative price.

item.title: ICVCM Core Carbon Principles: what institutional buyers need to know
item.description: The CCP framework in plain language — the ten principles, what the label changes in procurement, and where proprietary platform credits like CXF stand.
